text: Every element of America's homeland security plan is critical, because the terrorists are ruthless and resourceful - and we know they are preparing to attack us again.
explanation: Characterises the adversary with vice language — 'terrorists' who are 'ruthless' (merciless) — a moral evaluation of the enemy's character rather than a purely empirical claim; the definition expressly includes vice/terror language. Borderline, as it also serves a threat-assessment function.

text: o  each minister should prepare and publish a statement of the skills and roles sought for each board.
explanation: Administrative requirement that ministers publish statements of board skills and roles; procedural with no moral vocabulary.

text: We have had an unprecedented 16 years of continuous economic expansion.
explanation: Economic performance statistic (16 years of expansion); purely empirical per the negative clarification.

text: We want young New Zealanders to be able to join KiwiSaver and stay in it for their working lives.
explanation: Policy intention regarding KiwiSaver enrolment and retention; instrumental savings policy, no moral language.

text: • It has been four years since the Maori Commercial Settlement Act was passed, and most iwi are yet to receive any form of settlement from the Crown.
explanation: Factual claim that most iwi have not received settlements four years after the Act. Although it implies a grievance, the text itself is descriptive/statistical with no explicit moral vocabulary (unjust, owed, rights), so it is coded 0.

text: Those policies have placed the federal government in the driver’s seat,
explanation: Descriptive political claim about the federal government's position; no moral-evaluative language.

text: This has resulted in increased pressure in the health system and failed outcomes for healthcare staff, patients and the public.
explanation: Performance criticism citing system pressure and 'failed outcomes'; an evaluation of results, not a moral judgment — fits the negative clarification on factual/performance claims.

text: •  More than two in every three New  Zealanders  does unpaid work outside their  own households.
explanation: Statistical claim about unpaid work prevalence; purely descriptive.

text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: Administrative detail on how cadetships will count toward senior awards under the National Curriculum; technocratic.

text: That’s why President Obama and Democrats in Congress have enacted infrastructure investments that will
explanation: Incomplete partisan statement about infrastructure investments; instrumental economic framing, no moral vocabulary.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: Funding statistic for early childhood education; a factual spending claim per the negative clarification.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: Partisan criticism calling an organisation 'secretive'; a generic negative adjective about transparency without explicit moral vocabulary (e.g., dishonest, unjust), so coded 0 under the negative clarification.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: Policy instrument describing a price discount for certain users; purely administrative.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Partisan performance criticism about public education on cleaner fuels; instrumental, no moral-evaluative language.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: Tax statistic on the share of income paid by an average worker; purely empirical/fiscal.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: Descriptive statement about party co-leadership; no moral content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: Environmental target framing (zero-carbon Britain by 2050) and emissions constraint; technocratic target language without moral vocabulary.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: Regional development commitment ('alternative growth pole'); economic/technocratic language.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: Announces 'new rights for patients'; the codebook treats rights language as explicit moral vocabulary (definition and clarification a/d). Ambiguity noted: these are likely statutory rights, but the affirmation of rights for a group is coded 1.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: Economic argument that investment fails to recognise farmers' contribution to the economy; instrumental framing of contribution to output, with no fairness/desert vocabulary made explicit.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: Factual/instrumental recognition that adoption costs can be prohibitive; an affordability point without moral-evaluative language.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: Equality-of-access commitment framed instrumentally, with a descriptive reference to 'disadvantaged backgrounds' and no explicit moral vocabulary; matches the negative clarification on instrumental access arguments and descriptive references to vulnerable groups.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A neutral directive about allocating spending to sectors; purely instrumental budgeting language with no moral vocabulary, matching the negative clarification on neutral descriptions of programmes and funding.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A straightforward policy commitment on rail ownership; no moral-evaluative language, just an administrative/structural proposal (negative clarification: neutral description of policy instruments).

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Instrumental language about supporting land managers in delivering ecoservices; no moral vocabulary or ethical framing.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Describes services contributing to political and economic well-being; economic/instrumental framing with no moral content.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A neutral administrative observation about conflicting roles; no evaluative or moral language whatsoever.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational goal (world leader in sustainable environment) lacking explicit moral vocabulary; fits the negative clarification on aspirational visions lacking moral language.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: A fragment about promised investment in hospital buildings; purely instrumental funding language.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical lead-in to a question for an opponent; contains no moral vocabulary or evaluation.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: Domestic violence is a morally charged subject, but the text is instrumental ('new laws to crack down') with no moral-evaluative language; per the negative clarification on descriptive references to morally charged subjects, this is 0.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: A programme commitment (fruit and vegetable promotion in schools); purely instrumental, like the negative example on sports participation programmes.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: An administrative reporting requirement for boards; no moral content.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Frames expanded access to talking therapies instrumentally (recovery and return to work); no moral-evaluative language.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Instrumental resource reallocation for whānau development; no moral vocabulary.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A parental leave policy framed around giving parents 'more choice'; 'choice' here is instrumental policy content, not an appeal to freedom as a protected moral value, so coded 0.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: An efficiency/value-for-public-money argument ('wise use of public dollars'); fits the negative clarification on economic and fiscal arguments.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A statistical/fiscal claim about debt per household; purely empirical, no moral evaluation.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: 'Proud reputation' is a generic positive adjective attached to peacekeeping; per the negative clarification on generic positive adjectives without moral content, coded 0.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary: 'a fair legal system that respects the rights... of all Australians' — fairness, respect, and rights are all listed in clarification (a) as explicit moral vocabulary.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Invokes 'inequality' in the tax system as something to be 'eliminated'; equality/inequality is explicit moral vocabulary in clarification (a), and framing its removal as a goal is a moral evaluation, even though it coexists with tax policy content.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: A factual/legal statement that aid spending is enshrined in law; 'must pay' expresses legal obligation, not a moral imperative, and no moral vocabulary appears.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: A descriptive account of an MP introducing a bill to highlight tenant problems; descriptive reference to a policy problem without moral-evaluative language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A spending commitment for aged care beds; neutral programme description with no moral vocabulary.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Proposes policing structures and partnership between Gardaí and communities; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is aspirational but not moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: A fiscal pitch about saving money and cutting waste; economic argument per the negative clarification.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational vision ('best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old') lacking explicit moral vocabulary; fits the negative clarification on aspirational visions.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: An administrative reform to end automatic entitlements to state cars; instrumental, no moral language.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: A partisan attack questioning whether opponents can be 'trusted'; although trust borders on character evaluation, it functions here as a partisan slogan about reliability/credibility rather than explicit moral-evaluative vocabulary, and the baby-milk reference is instrumental; coded 0 with some ambiguity acknowledged.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: A procedural rule for TDs' legislative proposals; purely administrative.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Pledges to commemorate the Easter Rising 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' — honouring national forebears invokes patriotism and respect, virtue language listed in the definition and clarification (b).

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration framed purely around meeting 'economic needs'; economic/instrumental argument with no moral vocabulary.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Administrative goal of an accountability framework for schools; 'right' here means appropriate, not a moral rights claim.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Invokes the 'victory of free nations in the War on Terror'; appeals to freedom/liberty as a value being defended, which the clarification explicitly includes, and 'terror' appears in the definition's vice-language list.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: A procedural point about appropriate debate time; administrative, no moral content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: An enforcement appeal about recreational fishers policing poaching; instrumental rule-enforcement language without moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: A statistical claim about jobs created; purely empirical performance data per the negative clarification.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: 'Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland' is a neutral institutional objective without moral vocabulary.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: Describes dismantling a 'dysfunctional' health agency; 'dysfunctional' is a generic negative performance adjective, not moral evaluation.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical/operational criticism of a waste strategy (scale, efficiency, traffic); no moral vocabulary.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Aspirational economic transition language ('prosperous, decarbonized economy'); generic positive adjectives without moral content.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: An economic competitiveness target ('best place... to do business'); purely economic aspiration, no moral language.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: Explicitly invokes a 'fair share' of government revenue for regions; 'fair' is explicit moral vocabulary under clarification (a), making this a fairness-based distributive claim.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Statistics on sports participation and volunteering; empirical claims with no moral evaluation.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognises Māori enterprise's contribution to the economy; framed in economic-contribution terms without moral-evaluative vocabulary such as justice or dignity.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement the Military Covenant; references a policy instrument without itself using moral-evaluative language.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Argues the funding cap 'acts against new and smaller parties'; an instrumental fairness-adjacent description without explicit moral vocabulary like 'unfair', so coded 0.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Explicitly invokes 'fairness' — accusing Mr Howard of forgetting 'what fairness actually means'; fairness is core moral vocabulary under clarification (a).

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: A programme development commitment (parent education); purely instrumental with no moral language.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: A trade-enforcement pledge about anti-dumping cooperation; instrumental economic policy, no moral vocabulary.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: A commitment to equip and staff the Defence Forces for peacekeeping obligations; instrumental language about meeting international obligations, no moral evaluation.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
